strengths: Elegant theoretical insight that Shapley values depend exclusively on the odd component of the value function decomposition, with clean and rigorous proof
First general theoretical justification for paired sampling heuristic, resolving an open conjecture from Fumagalli et al. (2026) that was limited to low-order interactions
Clever application of Fourier basis where odd/even properties align with cardinality parity, enabling clean decomposition and efficient implementation
Maintains consistency guarantee (convergence to true Shapley values as m → 2^d) while improving computational complexity from O(d^k·m) to O((d + m/η)²m)
State-of-the-art empirical performance with lowest average rank (1.50) across 8 benchmarks; particularly strong improvements on moderate-to-high-dimensional problems (up to 62× error reduction)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablation studies and clear presentation of results with proper uncertainty quantification (median ± IQR)
Well-organized presentation with clear algorithm description and sound technical approach; all proofs appear correct
weaknesses: No finite-sample convergence rates or error bounds provided; only asymptotic consistency proven; unclear how approximation error scales with m, dimension d, and sparsity of true interactions

Critical dependence on GBT proxy model quality largely unanalyzed: no theoretical bounds on impact of proxy misspecification, false positive/negative rates in interaction selection, or robustness guarantees

Brief acknowledgment but insufficient exploration of even-odd correlation problem mentioned by Butler et al. (2025); discarding even components may lose information useful for odd approximation—impact not thoroughly investigated

Limited experimental scope: only d ≤ 101; no truly high-dimensional experiments (d >> 100); budgets m ≈ 100d not aggressive; low-budget regime (m < d·η) falls back to GBT and is underexplored; no comparison with higher-order PolySHAP (k ≥ 5)

Practical computational advantage unclear: while asymptotically better than PolySHAP, Figure 5 shows OddSHAP runtime comparable to RegressionMSR and substantially higher than LeverageSHAP; function evaluation (T_m) dominates regression cost, limiting practical benefit

Hyperparameter η lacks principled selection strategy: default η = 10 appears arbitrary; Figure 4 shows strong dataset dependence without clear guidance for practitioners to choose η without ground truth access
Missing finite-sample error analysis for approximation when true high-impact interactions are unknown; no bounds relating proxy quality to final Shapley value estimation error
No formal statistical significance testing; median ± IQR reported but unclear whether differences between methods are statistically significant when differences are small relative to IQR bands

strengths: Elegant core theoretical insight: Observation 3.1 that Shapley values depend exclusively on odd components is novel and well-presented, with a clean proof
Theoretical unification of paired sampling: Theorem 3.2 provides the first general justification for the widely-used paired sampling heuristic, resolving an open conjecture
Sound mathematical development: Theorems 3.2-3.5 are carefully proven; Lemma 3.4 on Fourier-unanimity equivalence is particularly useful
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 8 datasets with varying dimensions, multiple budget levels, ablation studies, and runtime analysis
Clear presentation: Well-organized writing with effective figures (particularly Figure 1) that communicate main ideas
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: OddSHAP combines existing techniques (paired sampling, GBT proxies, polynomial regression); restricting to odd-order Fourier terms is a straightforward application of the core insight rather than a novel algorithmic contribution

Modest and inconsistent empirical improvements: On low-dimensional datasets (d≤16), OddSHAP performs identically to RegressionMSR; improvements only appear consistently for d≥30 without clear explanation for this dependency
No computational advantage: Figure 5 shows OddSHAP has higher runtime than RegressionMSR; theoretical complexity O((d+m/η)²m) is still expensive and dominated by regression cost at large budgets

Substantial gap between theory and practice: Theoretical consistency (Theorem 3.5) applies to full regression; practical algorithm uses sparse proxy-selected interactions, introducing approximation error and proxy bias with no finite-sample error analysis provided

Critical limitation inadequately addressed: Authors acknowledge that even-odd interactions may be correlated (undermining odd-only restriction) but provide no investigation of when this occurs or solutions to mitigate it
Hyperparameter sensitivity: Figure 4 shows substantial sensitivity to η with no principled selection method; limited guidance on setting this parameter in practice
Incomplete comparisons: 3-PolySHAP results missing for 5/8 datasets; no formal statistical significance testing or confidence intervals reported
Narrow experimental scope: Only feature attribution evaluated despite mentioning data valuation and causal inference; maximum dimension d=101 raises questions about high-dimensional scaling

strengths: Novel theoretical insight: Shapley values depend exclusively on the odd component of value functions, providing elegant mathematical foundation and natural motivation for the approach
Significant theoretical contribution: First rigorous justification for paired sampling heuristic (Theorem 3.2), resolving an open conjecture and explaining why this widely-used technique works
Mathematically sound: All theorems are technically correct with rigorous proofs; Fourier basis perspective cleanly separates odd/even components where χ_T is odd iff |T| is odd

Well-designed practical algorithm: Thoughtfully combines paired sampling, Fourier basis decomposition, GBT-based interaction detection, and sparse regression to maintain consistency while avoiding PolySHAP's O(d^{2k}m) complexity

Strong empirical performance: Achieves state-of-the-art results with lowest average rank (1.50) across benchmarks; substantial improvements on moderate-to-high dimensional problems (d≥30), e.g., 62× error reduction on Cancer dataset

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 8 diverse datasets, multiple baselines with fair comparison, extensive ablations, runtime analysis with simulated evaluation costs, and reproducible setup with code provided
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective motivating figures, logical flow from theoretical insight to practical algorithm, detailed proofs and extended results in appendices
weaknesses: Limited practical improvements on small-dimensional problems: Performance on low-d datasets (d=14-16) is merely comparable to RegressionMSR, not superior; main benefits only materialize at d≥30, limiting applicability to many real-world feature attribution tasks

Unproven sparsity assumption: Effectiveness critically depends on value functions being well-approximated by sparse odd-order Fourier interactions; while empirically validated, no theoretical characterization is provided for when this holds

Weak hyperparameter guidance: Factor η is set to 10 throughout without principled justification; Figure 4 shows overfitting for small η but provides limited problem-specific selection guidance; threshold m < d·η for TreeSHAP fallback appears arbitrary

Inconsistent and unexplained results: Estate dataset shows 'outlier improvements' and is omitted from Figure 4 without detailed investigation, raising concerns about stability or sensitivity to problem structure

Incremental algorithmic contributions: While theoretical insights are novel, the algorithm combines existing techniques (paired sampling, Fourier basis from FourierSHAP, GBT proxies, sparse regression); novelty is primarily in applying these to the odd subspace

Missing convergence analysis: No sample complexity bounds, convergence rates, or finite-sample error guarantees provided; consistency is established but tighter theoretical analyses would strengthen claims

Limited experimental scope: Only 8 datasets with maximum dimension d=101; lacks high-dimensional experiments (d>200) where sparsity benefits might be most pronounced or evaluation on very sparse functions

Runtime overhead not always justified: OddSHAP runtime is similar to RegressionMSR and sometimes higher than LeverageSHAP (Figure 5); regression cost O(|T|²m) becomes substantial at larger budgets, making cost-benefit analysis unclear except for large-d problems

Proxy model dependency: Interaction detection quality depends on GBT approximation; with tight budgets near m≈d·η threshold, proxy may be poorly fit, potentially missing important interactions; regime switch to TreeSHAP creates discontinuity
